notes.title: December Patchnotes #1
notes.content:
Greetings Adventurers,

the December patch is here! After the big 0.8 Version launch, we've been closely listening to your feedback, fixing bugs, and adding improvements based on your feedback on Discord!

Here are the fixes, additions & improvements for this month's patch: 

[list]
[*][b] 💾Added a new check to detect unsaved map changes when editing characters during map building:[/b]
Players will now get a warning to save their map changes when editing characters without fear of losing their map-building progress. This new safeguard ensures your hard work on maps remains intact, even if you need to tweak your miniatures mid-session.

[*] [b]🖌️Fixed an issue causing the map brush to get stuck when switching to the character editor:[/b]
Editing characters during map building will now behave as intended, disabling the brush inside the character editor.

[*][b]🔊 Adjusted sound mixing for the tutorial[/b]
Adjusted the loudness of various sound files during the tutorial mission.

[*][b]🧟 Reintroduced the Zombie Soldier and Undead Fighter miniatures to the map builder[/b]
Back by popular demand (or better said: fixed thanks to your reports)! The undead are once again available for all your necromantic (or apocalyptic) encounter designs. 

[*][b]🔧 Fixed a Bug where the character editor UI was sometimes not visible in VR[/b]
[/list]

We’re constantly working to improve the game and your feedback is invaluable, so keep it coming! 
Stay tuned for more updates in future releases!

And as always: 
[b]See you inside Dungeon Full Dive![/b]

We’re thrilled to announce that the highly anticipated 0.8 Update is officially here!

Packed with exciting new features, fresh assets, major improvements, and fixes, this update is brimming with content! Among the highlights are two major additions that you’ve been eagerly awaiting:

[b]1. The upgraded character sheets
2. The all-new tutorial mission[/b]

If you’ve been waiting to upgrade your TTRPG adventures, now is the perfect time to dive in!
https://store.steampowered.com/app/1710740/Dungeon_Full_Dive_Game_Master_Edition/

The character and monster sheets have received major upgrades in version 0.8!

[list]
[*] [b]Select your action and press "Use":[/b] The roll-to-hit is automatically calculated for you.

[h3]The Stylish Hairstyle[/h3]
[img]https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/42258170/07cd9697bfdecee702a4285149e4804c9851d12d.jpg[/img]
[i]"Some of you may die, but it's a sacrifice I am willing to make."[/i]
Evil lord or common villager? Either way, those stylish bangs will have heads turning!

[h2]🆕More Features, Improvements, and Fixes![/h2]

With the launch of the 0.8 Update, a wide variety of new features and improvements have been introduced. Here’s the full list:

[list]
[*] [b]Added a new map-saving system that detects changes automatically and asks you to save[/b]
[img]https://clan.fastly.steamstatic.com/images/42258170/16f6e154342baa95e07e19708e10e89305e9712b.jpg[/img] [i]Never lose your map-building progress again! This feature ensures your hard work is always saved.[/i]

[i]Spells now use the correct spell slots and scale the damage dice accordingly, adding more flexibility to your spellcasting![/i]

notes.title: Sneak Preview: The upcoming Update 0.8!
notes.content:
[h2][b]Greetings, Adventurer![/b][/h2]

Over the past weeks and months, we've been hard at work on [b]major new features[/b] and various improvements based on your feedback (yes, we're looking at you, Discord community!). Today, we're thrilled to [b]officially announce Update 0.8[/b]!

[hr][/hr]

[h1]🆕 What to Expect in Update 0.8[/h1]

[h2]📝 Rollable, Automated Attacks and Spells[/h2]

One of the most exciting additions in Update 0.8 is the introduction of [b]rollable Attacks and Spells[/b].


[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/42258170/08b936d8c840a8a33e0cfb341802dc0f6a20f5ac.jpg[/img][i]Barbarians, rejoice! Even less math needed to play DFD![/i]
[list] 
[*]Want to roll an attack? Just press "Attack," and your proficiency is automatically calculated. 
[*]Need to roll damage? It’s just one click away! 
[*]Casting a spell? The damage roll is automatically determined based on the spell level! 
[/list]We are continuously working on the automation side of things for DFD and we are looking forward to hearing your feedback on these upcoming first steps towards this direction.

[h2]🧝A Singleplayer Mission for Beginners?![/h2]

Wait, what? Singleplayer? Can I now play DFD without a GM? Well... yes and no.

Based on the feedback from our recent Player Survey, [b]many of you have been asking[/b]  for a tutorial. So, in Update 0.8, we've prepared something special just for you:

[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/42258170/8bc4bc9039af933128b1bfed4756c9c7272f2ec9.jpg[/img]
We've added a [b]brand-new Singleplayer Beginner's Mission[/b] designed to provide new players with an excellent introduction to DFD and its tools!

For our seasoned players, we're also working on adding additional tooltips and information that can be accessed during gameplay.

[hr][/hr]
[h1]🔔When Will Update 0.8 Be Released?[/h1]

Update 0.8 is currently in full-force development, and we're aiming for a release in [b]Q4 this year[/b]—specifically, this November.

Stay tuned as we share more details as we get closer to the release date!

[hr][/hr]
[h1]What Else Can You Expect from Update 0.8?[/h1]

But wait… there's more! You can also look forward to:

[h3]🐺 New Miniatures[/h3]
[h3]🐺 New Character Assets[/h3]
[h3]...and yes, even more features waiting to be unveiled![/h3]

So, keep your eyes peeled on our social media and Discord for sneak peeks of what's to come in Update 0.8.

See you inside DFD!

notes.title: 📢Chapter 3 is OUT NOW! 📢
notes.content:
[h2]Chapter 3 is out now![/h2]

Greetings Adventurer and Welcome to Chapter 3! 

As always, this update was made based on your feedback and we're excited to show you all the changes, new features, and improvements that made it into this first update of Chapter 3!

Before we dive deep into the details of Chapter 3, we wanted to say a big thank you for your support!

[h2]🆓Free Player Edition[/h2]
Also, don't forget that starting with chapter 3 (on the 12th of April), all Players can [b]start playing for FREE[/b] by downloading the [b]Player Edition[/b]! 

Learn more about the free Player Edition over here:

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2839600/Dungeon_Full_Dive_Player_Edition/

[h1]🆕 What’s New in Chapter 3?[/h1]

[h2]🎲New Features[/h2]
[h3]Miniature Overview List[/h3]
As a GM, the Miniature Overview List allows you to easily keep track of all the miniatures on the table. With it, you can now:
[list]
[*] Jump to the location of miniatures
[*] Keep track of HP of miniatures
[*] Quick-Access character sheets
[*] Quick-Access Full Dive
[*] Quickly add & remove miniatures to the Combat Initiative
[/list]
[img]https://clan.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/images/42258170/ae7023ca1191af716b3b6e5e5c256b1c80406bf9.gif[/img]
For players (Non-GMs), this list is automatically filtered to only display the party members.
[h3]New Healthbar System in Tabletop Mode[/h3]
The new system for healthbars now only displays HP bars in tabletop mode when hovering over a miniature.
[img]https://clan.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/images/42258170/58d5b9341b926f8479709b8340ff9be7ec905f40.gif[/img]
As a GM you can switch between the following settings for your Players:
[list]
[*] [b]Full For All:[/b] All Players (Non-GMs) can see the HP bar on hover, including the exact number values.
[*][b] Exact Numbers Only For GM:[/b] Players will only see the HP bar but no exact numbers
[*] [b]Only For GM:[/b] Players will have no info displayed when hovering miniatures
[/list]
[img]https://clan.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/images/42258170/77792f5e7e1e9ed5ac6051f45a0db1e6e91e1c71.jpg[/img]
[h3]Undo / Redo Tool for Mapbuilder[/h3]
The highly requested Undo/Redo Tool has been added to the mapbuilder! It allows you to undo OR redo your last map building actions. 
[img]https://clan.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/images/42258170/a23abb7acd4466fa5c97adea9b215d90427116fc.gif[/img]
[h3]Customizeable World & Player View[/h3]
A new setting has been added to the options: With the world & player visibility setting you can now choose to hide the table and/or the other players depending on your personal preferences.
[img]https://clan.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/images/42258170/037bfe00c986dfb12db0ca2db993b0543289b1d2.gif[/img]

[h2]⚙️Improved Code Modding Support[/h2]
[list]
[*]The coding backend of DFD has been changed from IL2CPP to Mono for better mod support. [*]Additionally, a first wiki on how to mod DFD was created You can check it out over [url=https://dungeonfulldive.notion.site/Dungeon-Full-Dive-Modding-6667f2dda86845559a44011507ca9825?pvs=4]HERE[/url].
[/list]
[h2]🎵New Music[/h2]
A new dynamic song has been added to the soundboard! As always, it includes 3 levels of intensity for your GM to dynamically adjust depending on the flow of the campaign. 
[olist]
[*] Tavern Music
[/olist]
[h2]🎨New Assets[/h2]
[h3]New Wizard Outfit for humanoid species[/h3]
The new wizard outfit is here! It includes a new hat, a new chest piece, new gauntlets, and new boots!
[img]https://clan.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/images/42258170/f0c48c375fec079ab3763d199d04e55753651d39.jpg[/img]
[h3]6 Clothing Sets for Dragonborns[/h3]
Six new clothing sets have been added for the Dragonborn species! 
[i][b]Disclaimer: [/b]Dragonborn characters that have been created before the Chapter 3 Update must be reconfigured in the Character Editor to work correctly with the new version of the game.[/i]
[img]https://clan.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/images/42258170/00f730473765713553fc0010dd2efb636af1546a.jpg[/img]
[h3]8 new eye sets for Dragonborns[/h3]
Eight new eye sets have been added to the Dragonborn species,
[h3]2 new horns for Dragonborns[/h3]
You can now choose between two different sets of horns as Dragonborn. 
[img]https://clan.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/images/42258170/49cea42a245daa6b757bf7f7f1dbc98122a8da94.jpg[/img]
[h3]New GM Dice Set[/h3]
As part of the GM Edition Upgrade, all Players have been rewarded with the GM Edition exclusive "Game Master" Dice set. 
[img]https://clan.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/images/42258170/d84b2c6c09e7f804eb19408b0ddf62d14550fea3.jpg[/img]
[h3]New Lorekeeper Dice Set[/h3]
A new dice set has been added that can be [b]unlocked for free[/b] by participating in the lorekeeper community event. 
You can check it out over [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1710740/view/4216006291758937798]HERE[/url].
[img]https://clan.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/images/42258170/87e72117b7497b1d01721356641007bddca943e1.jpg[/img]
[h1]🛠️ Additional Improvements [/h1]
We have also been doing a lot of miscellaneous improvements on existing features as well as bug fixes. Here is the complete overview of the changes and fixes:
[h2]Additional Improvements[/h2]
[list]
    [*] New Main Menu design, Play Screen design, animation & music
    [*] Improved smoothing brush for terraforming
[img]https://clan.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/images/42258170/3541d944228586722fbf6b8d4b8dea813bf7757b.gif[/img]
    [*] Added new sound effects for the character editor, map building, UI interactions, and item usages
    [*] While in tabletop mode PC players are now prevented from going too far out of bounds. 
    [*] Added an indication when players are attempting to mapbuild outside of the current table area
    [*] Dice are now bigger in PC & VR and scale with you in VR
    [*] Added animation when placing map assets
    [*] TOTW Oneshot maps are now marked as official

[/list]
[h2]Resolved Bugs[/h2]
[list]
    [*] Fixed characters not correctly reacting to the light depending on the selected mood setting
    [*] Fixed duplicate ID issues on official maps which caused network interactions not to be shown correctly for certain objects
    [*] Fixed terrain issues where terrain disappeared after going into full dive from terraforming
    [*] Fixed frame lags in Miniature Browser & Map Browser UIs. You can now browse the mapbrowser even while it's loading new maps.
    [*] Fixed character sheet unintentionally opening when writing in chat
    [*] Fixed Voice Chat Indicator overlay not correctly showing in PC
    [*] Fixed an issue where the only available character was a bear and no new characters could be created
[/list]

[h1]❤️ Thank you[/h1]

We've really put our hearts into the first update of Chapter 3, wanting to make it something special. But honestly, we couldn't have done any of this without your support. So, a huge thank you from all of us here. Your support is what keeps us going and makes all the difference in pushing DFD to the next level!

[b]See you inside Dungeon Full Dive![/b]

[h3]Discuss this update on Discord[/h3]
[url=https://discord.gg/e8FznWcyxk][img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/42258170/d776b95ce3951c6b6035941e94c532768f156bd1.gif[/img][/url]

notes.title: Announcing: FREE DFD Player Edition!
notes.content:
[h1][b]Greetings Travellers,[/b][/h1]
Today marks a big milestone in the journey of Dungeon Full Dive: We’ve been reading through forums, comments, reviews, direct messages, gathering all your feedback and wishes. You’ve made it clear what you want, and we've been on a mission to make it happen. So, here’s the big news we’ve all been waiting for:

[h2][b]🌟 DFD: Player Edition - Free for all Adventurers[/b][/h2]
Yes, you read that right. After many weeks of testing, going through player feedback, and thinking about how to make it work: We're finally ready to unveil the [b]DFD: Player Edition[/b].
[b]DFD: Player Edition[/b] is a free version of Dungeon Full Dive designed specifically for players. This edition will allow you to experience the magic of DFD, join online tabletop sessions, and embark on TTRPG adventures. And the best part? [b]It’s absolutely free.[/b]

[h3]What's in the free Player Edition?[/h3][list][*][b]Play Online:[/b] Play TTRPG online with your friends or with people you meet online.[/*][*][b]Create your Character:[/b] Create your own miniatures and 5e characters.[/*][*][b]Build Your own Worlds:[/b] Build your own maps.[/*][*][b]Test GM Tools:[/b] Explore the full set of DFD’s GM tools in offline play.[/*][/list][h3]What’s [u]not[/u] available in the free Player Edition?[/h3][list][*]Hosting Games will be limited to the GM Edition of DFD.[/*][*]Players of the Player Edition will not be able to take on the role of the GM during online play.[/*][*]Character Creation will be limited to 3 slots while Map Building will be limited to 2 slots.[/*][/list]
[h2][b]🎲 DFD becomes “DFD: Game Masters Edition”[/b][/h2]
Simultaneously, the current version of DFD will transition into the “DFD: GM Edition” [b]and its price will be increased from $29 to $49 once the Player Edition is released.[/b] This price change allows us to focus on enhancing the overall value of GM edition as much as possible while at the same time making DFD more accessible for groups to dive into the DFD universe together, reducing the entry cost for a party of 5 from $150 to $49.

Additionally, as a special bonus all owners of the GM edition will be given [b]an exclusive GM dice set[/b].

[b]What happens if I already own Dungeon Full Dive when the Player Edition releases?[/b]
If you already own DFD prior to the release of the Player Edition, your game will automatically be upgraded to the GM Edition at no additional cost. You'll retain full access to all the features you've enjoyed, along with any new GM-specific enhancements and content introduced in the GM Edition.

[b]Can I buy the GM Version now while it's still cheaper?[/b]
Yes, you have the opportunity to purchase the GM Edition at the current price before the Player Edition is released and the price increase takes effect. This allows you to lock in the full range of GM features and future updates at a more favorable price point.

[h1][b]🎉The Player Edition Steam Page is LIVE![/b][/h1]
The Steam page for DFD: Player Edition has been launched [b]right now[/b]. Head over to wishlist!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2839600/

Want to support us and spread the word? Share this with your friends and gaming communities!

[h2][b]🔍 Looking Ahead[/b][/h2]
The Player Edition reflects our commitment to making Dungeon Full Dive accessible to a wider audience while providing specialized tools for those who craft the adventures. We believe these changes will enrich the DFD experience for everyone, creating a more vibrant and diverse community of adventurers and storytellers.

Stay tuned for more details on the release date and features of the DFD: Player Edition. We're just as excited as you are to embark on this new chapter together!

Thank you for your continued support and passion. We can't wait to see the adventures you'll embark on.

[b]Happy adventuring,[/b]

The TxK Gaming Studios Team



[h1][b]❓Open Questions? We made this FAQ![/b][/h1]
[b]Why the free Player Edition?[/b]
[list][*]The free Player Edition is introduced to make Dungeon Full Dive (DFD) more accessible to a broader audience. It's designed to lower the entry barrier for new players, allowing them to experience the game without any financial commitment. At the same time our goal is to make it more accessible for groups to dive into the DFD universe together, significantly reducing the entry cost for a party.[/*][/list]
[b]What is the difference between the Player Edition and the GM Edition?[/b]
[list][*]Check out our overview graphic for an easy comparison between the Player and GM edition:
[img]https://clan.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/images/42258170/78463f3e9956607c2a7a6554e4224a5c742a6454.png[/img][/*][/list]
[b]When will the Player Edition be released?[/b]
[list][*]Details on the specific release date for the Player Edition will be announced soon. For now, stay tuned to the official DFD channels and wishlist the Player Edition on Steam to stay up to date.[/*][/list]
[b]Why will the GM version become more expensive?[/b]
[list][*]The price adjustment for the GM Edition reflects the enhanced value and comprehensive features it offers. This change is part of our strategy to make the overall DFD experience more accessible while ensuring that dedicated Game Masters have access to an extensive suite of tools and capabilities. The new pricing model also supports the continued development and expansion of DFD, ensuring a rich and evolving gameplay experience for all users.[/*][/list]

The TxK Gaming Studios Team

notes.content:
[h1]This is it.[/h1]

[h2]Chapter 2: The GM Update is [b]out now for everyone[/b] to play![/h2]

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1710740/Dungeon_Full_Dive/

Chapter 2 is DFD’s [b]most ambitious and biggest update[/b] yet. This update was made based on your feedback and requests and there are a LOT of changes, new features, and improvements.

So much, that Rachel and Lyria have even prepared [b]a special video for you all[/b] just for this update and to go over what’s new in Chapter 2.

So be sure to check it out!

[previewyoutube=HlDA3aURJ44;full][/previewyoutube]

[h1]🎉 Celebrate with 20% Off & Free Player Demo![/h1]

Before we dive deep into the details of Chapter 2, we wanted to say a big thank you for your support!

As a thank you and to celebrate the kickoff of chapter 2, we're offering an exclusive [b]20% discount on DFD until next week only (December 11th)[/b]!

Plus, don't forget that you can have a sneak peek of Chapter 2 with your entire party by downloading the [b]Free Player Demo[/b]. Unsure yet if you want to dive in with the whole group? Only during December, you have the chance to experience the excitement of DFD for free! Learn more about the limited demo [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1710740/view/3904119881299041920][here][/url].

[h1]🆕 What’s New in Chapter 2?[/h1]

[h2]🎲New Features[/h2]

[h3]Music & Ambience Board[/h3]
[previewyoutube=YdTDa8FbVYE;full][previewyoutube=YdTDa8FbVYE;leftthumb][/previewyoutube][/previewyoutube]
You can now add music and ambience sounds to your game with our new Music & Ambience Board. On top of that: Each ambience and music track also has an intensity slider so you can customize your listening experience:

A little rain can turn into a massive storm, or distant wolf howls can suddenly feel like they're right next to you.
Is your party low on health and about to go down? Crank up the intensity! The music changes at your demand.

[h3]Fog of War[/h3]
[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/42258170/fdd297b36997874d27bce55a5378206affe10585.gif[/img]
You can now add Fog of War to your Maps to hide enemies or map parts. As a GM these blocks are see through but as a player they are pitch black …until a player moves their miniature inside it that is.

[h3]Animations in Tabletop Mode[/h3]
[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/42258170/13947a0d90b8ae66b4e786d8880e12cb640c113e.gif[/img]
We have now added the ability to show animation even when in tabletop mode. This means your GM can now stay in full control in tabletop mode while still seeing what the party is up to.

[h3]Initiative Tracker & HP Bars[/h3]
The new Initiative tracker allows your GM to start an encounter at any time. By pressing the “Start Combat” button inside the new miniature overview tab. This will open the “Combat Preparation” Window where all participants for the encounter can be selected.
[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/42258170/4834ff07685ff5b6d24672e419df585012a4102b.jpg[/img]
Starting combat will spawn the Initiative Tracker for everyplayer. In here the GM can go through the turn order by using the “End Turn” Button.
[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/42258170/0eaa1481c079b7b3975571577050f5afa56fbbaa.jpg[/img]

[h3]HP Bars[/h3]
We have also added the ability to show HP bars so that you can easily keep track of the HP of all miniatures on the board.
This setting can be configured under the “Settings” menu in the Pause Menu. Here you can currently toggle between enabled and disabled. (More settings are planned)
[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/42258170/0ddd28ac75e3d41fe652210b7d1b78c650405401.png[/img]
[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/42258170/46b838f7a37ced5d6a60e3dad3a96d8ab2a6672a.png[/img]
[h3]Enhanced Character Sheets[/h3]
Dive deeper into your character's capabilities with the new improved Character Sheet, now displaying your:

[list]
[*]Class / Species
[*]Actions & Abilities
[*]Spells
[*]Equipment
[/list]

[b]Spells[/b]
In the new spells tab, you can now manage your character's spells. The spell sheets include the entire 5e OGL spell library for you to use. And: You can also cast spells directly from the tab, which automatically tracks your spell slots for you and shares the spell descriptions with your party in the chat.
[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/42258170/12640ca23f85c7c592999e4cb30ec9a0079fe08e.jpg[/img]

[b]Actions, Features & Traits[/b]
The new actions tab lets you keep track of all the actions your character can unleash individualized based on your character class and equipped gear.
Also, you are able to look at the features & traits provided by your class and species.
[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/42258170/6ae58beca877b57c03b2029d592f5c237798d4f0.jpg[/img]

[b]Inventory[/b]
In the Inventory page, you can manage your character’s equipment as well as keep track of your parties gold.
[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/42258170/784b5dbc03e098943683e098a4da9eac0afb6674.png[/img]

[b]Stats Page Overhaul[/b]
We have improved the current stats page: You can now select your class, subclass as well as species and subspecies. On top of that, we have also polished the general UI Design.
[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/42258170/834d254de348424f4da0f8843e5311275ce0c55d.jpg[/img]

[b]Character Customization[/b]
Next to the content of the 5e OGL library (using the https://dnd.wizards.com/resources/systems-reference-document), you are able to add your own content to the game as well!
For more info and an in-depth explanation, we will be adding tutorials in the following days over [url=https://dungeonfulldive.notion.site/Modding-8b7b878c1d764a3d92f84c859c609a6b?pvs=4]HERE[/url].

[h3]Jumping[/h3]
[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/42258170/d59e02a805bbffa7e93d0d6a7764663a3a109ad1.gif[/img]
Hep Hep, you can now jump inside DFD when Full Diving. We look forward to the first parcour maps!

[h3]Instruments[/h3]
The following instruments are now playable in VR and on PC:
[list]
[*]Horn
[*]Harp
[*]Lute (Improved Audio)
[/list]

[h3]Body Sliders[/h3]
[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/42258170/b43f3c7b05e8ad1c6f7a1fb966aaa9632260f233.gif[/img]
You can now customize the body parts of your character using the new body slider tab! From long-necked wizards to chonky Barbarians, let your imagination go wild!

If you want to customize your character’s appearance even more, you can now change the available skin colors within the config files.
For a detailed tutorial, check out our tutorial [url=https://www.notion.so/dungeonfulldive/Modding-Character-Data-8b7b878c1d764a3d92f84c859c609a6b]HERE[/url]

notes.title: Announcing Chapter 2!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42258170/3b409ca36f225d3d3c00ecce379b76b02b20e8ec.png[/img]
It's time to talk about roadmap.

We've heard your tales, we've listened to your feedback and we've shared our development plans with you. Meanwhile, we've also been working on our [b]most ambitious and biggest updates[/b] yet. So, we're extremely excited to announce:

[h1]✨Chapter 2 is coming!✨[/h1]

[b]Chapter 2 is all about bringing the best possible experience to your GMs & making it as easy as possible for you to play your favorite TTRPG![/b]

With Chapter 2 we are focusing on adding features and improvements that allow you to play and most importantly [b]host[/b] your tabletop games as easily as possible. 
This includes [b]new GM tools, deeper stat integration for 5e[/b], and of course [b]more TTRPG features[/b]!
At the same time, we want to push what is possible inside DFD by bringing you [b]more assets, new species[/b], and many other [b]new features[/b] that you have been asking for!

[h1]The Three Pillars of Chapter 2[/h1]

[h2]🛠️1. GM Tools[/h2]
Prepare yourselves for brand new Game Master controls! We're giving your GMs a variety of new tools to control the campaigns, adjust the flow of play, and navigate through combat. Exciting features await as your GM takes control of the story with new and improved features such as [b]Fog of War[/b], [b]Advanced Miniature Management[/b], and much more!

[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/42258170/92b9b345047f7f56dc434b8b254f9bf1afb3eac5.gif[/img][i]What could be hiding here? A small Teaser of the upcoming Fog of War Tool.[/i]

[h2]⚔️2. Basic Combat[/h2]
Combat is a cornerstone of every tabletop session, so we are adding new tools to make combat even more enjoyable for the whole party! New features like [b]Automated Initiative Tracking[/b] will make your Combat sessions focus on the action instead of lengthy calculations. At the same time, our new [b]Character Sheets[/b] and the inclusion of [b]ALL the 5e Monster Stat Sheets[/b] in the OGL will give you and your GM complete access to every information that you'll need while fighting through your encounters! Take a first step into the exciting realm of combat with us and we look forward to your feedback as you charge into your battles inside DFD!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42258170/8bdf12595c060262ffcfd35492f82b9dba38c335.png[/img][i]Behold my mighty Spell Book! The current Design of the Spells Tab.[/i]

[h2] 🐉3. EVEN MORE Variety [/h2]
We want every player to completely immerse themselves in their campaign like never before. So, we are adding new [b]battle maps[/b], even [b]more map assets[/b], and new features to [b]make your worlds more interactable while Full Diving[/b]. At the same time, we are also giving players brand [b]new ways to customize[/b] their characters with [b]more in-depth body customization[/b] and yes,[b] a brand new species! [/b]
[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/42258170/4dcf07dc83f97e3076c2e103ab4ca2c93b97f08d.png[/img][i]Roll for Seduction. Work in Progress of the New Dragonborn Species.[/i]

[h1]The Roadmap of Chapter 2[/h1]

Chapter 2 will be kicked off with a [b]MAJOR update on December 4th[/b]. After that, we will sequentially add [b]more and more of the features[/b] and improvements as we closely listen to your feedback.

Check out our Roadmap with a selection (not all!) of  the planned features for the updates of Chapter 2:
[url=https://portal.productboard.com/dungeonfulldive/1-dungeon-full-dive-portal/tabs/2-planned-in-progress][img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/42258170/28499597d9596ad16704d9406d0f61344c233426.png[/img][/url][i]Visit our Roadmap Page to cast your Vote for Prioritization![/i]

[h1]📅25 days until Chapter 2 Kicks off![/h1]

We’re immensely grateful for your support as we kick off the next milestone in DFD's development road. 
With Chapter 2 we plan to [b]bring the GM experience to the next level[/b] [u]one update at a time[/u]. And while there’s still work to be done, we are incredibly excited to make DFD the best TTRPG experience possible for you!

We haven’t nearly spoiled everything yet, though! Stay tuned as we reveal more content, [b]insights, and in-depth dev blogs in the coming days[/b] and weeks as we reveal the full depth of Chapter 2. Until then:

[h1]Get ready for December the 4th[/h1]

notes.title: Dungeon Full Dive Devlog #2: Crafting an Immersive Sound Design
notes.content:
Greetings Adventurers!


Our Development Team is always working hard to give you the most immersive experience in Dungeon Full Dive. So, today, we will show you the latest advances from our Sound Design department and how it makes your sessions feel like you’re in the worlds you have created!

Hear us out (pun intended). You are going to love this!

[h2]Collision Sounds[/h2]
When fighting adversities, or getting a bit funky in the tavern, your weapons could stumble against other objects.
What happens at that moment? Our Collision System will activate!

Our system defines a “Collisionobject” and “Collisionsurface” when a collision occurs. The former determines which kind of sound will be produced; for example, if you are swinging a sword, the noise will be metallic. And the latter, on the other hand, determines where the object is landing, like a wooden table.
The result will be the sound that you will perceive in your headset.

Pretty cool, right? But that’s not all!

Our Collision Sound system has A LOT of different combinations that will make your sessions as immersive as ever!

Let’s imagine that our Collisionobject is a Sword, and the Collisionsurface is a wooden mug. If our sword hits the cup, we will hear the sound of metal hitting wood. However, if it’s the mug hitting the sword the sound produced will be different, since wood hitting metal makes a different vibration for our ears!

What if two Collisionobject, like a sword and a wooden mace, clash? Well, the sound produced will be based on the first object hit, so if the sword is faster at the time of impact, our system will register it as the Collisionobject, while the mace becomes our surface!

[h2]Sound Parameters[/h2]
When fighting for our lives against the coolest enemy the DM’s twisted mind created, we need to feel like we are in our fantasy world and living the battle. But how can we hear the correct audio feedback in our actions? Well, that’s where our Sound Parameters start gearing up!
The sound produced is based on three parameters: Loudness, location, and threshold.
Loudness means the intensity of the sound, based on impact speed. Location tells us where the sound is coming from. And Threshold refers to the minimum strength required to activate that sound.

Just like in the real world, in the fantasy landscapes that we will fight on, we will hear our sound reception based on how hard we are hitting our enemies, the direction the sound is coming from, and if it’s there is enough strength to create an audible sound, or maybe we are too far away to grasp it.

And that’s it for Devlog #2! 
We can’t wait to hear (no pun intended, again) your feedback on our progress and all of your questions, Adventurers!

Excited about what’s next? Follow us on our Socials and join our [url=https://discord.gg/4PX7SUU5UB]Discord Community[/url] to be the first one to know about the latest DfD news!

notes.title: Our Character Editor! #2 - Developer Update
notes.content:
[h2][b]Our Character Editor! #2 - Dressed for the occasion[/b][/h2]
[b]Greetings Travelers! [/b]

Welcome back to our latest developer update and the second part of the [b]character editor[/b] [b]insight series[/b], in which we are giving you a look behind the curtains of our character art pipeline as well as its main challenge: Creating a [b]gorgeous-looking[/b], visual art style for our characters, while at the same time meeting the[b] strict performance goals[/b] that we set ourselves (to ensure good performance for all of our players). 

While in the last part of the series ([url=https://txkgaming.com/uncategorized/our-character-editor-1-development-update/]#1 The visual art challenge: Bringing your heroes to life[/url]), we investigated the visuals of our characters, in this part we will focus on the [b]features of the character editor[/b] as well as the [b]technical details[/b] that come along with it. 

[b]So, let’s dive right into it! [/b]

[h2][b]The Technical Setup [/b][/h2]
To build the fundamentals of our character editor, we first had to determine the parts of the character that we wanted to be able to modify. So, we started by defining separate regions on the characters' face and their body, that should be [b]swappable[/b]. These regions include [b]body features like hair, eyes, and ears[/b], as well as[b] clothing[/b] such as [b]chest[/b] [b]pieces, gauntlets, or boots. [/b]
[img]https://txkgaming.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/image-1.png[/img][i]Barbarian clothing zones[/i]

Another fundamental decision that we made for our character editor was that the [b]clothing pieces should fit all classes[/b]:

[u]If a wizard wants to wear heavy chainmail, why not let them?[/u] 

Now, with our zones identified, we were able to [b]swap out each of them individually[/b]. In theory, our characters can now mix and match their outfits with different hairstyles, chest pieces, boots, gauntlets, etc.

[b]Character editor completed & adventure finished? [/b]
Sadly, far from it! With this system in place there are two main issues that still exist and need solving:
[olist][*][b]Layered clothing [/b][/*][/olist][olist][*][b]Performance [/b][/*][/olist]
So, let’s take a deeper look into these two problems: [b]Why do they exist and how did we solve them?[/b] 

[h2][b]Layered clothing [/b][/h2]
When we compare our existing barbarian design with the design of this monk over here, we can already see one [b]fundamental difference:[/b] 

[img]https://txkgaming.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/MonkZonesComparedColoredLines-1024x655.png[/img][i]Barbarian vs Monk > Clothing zones compared[/i]

The zones we have defined for the barbarian are [b]completely[/b] [b]different[/b] [b]in size [/b]compared to the monk. Not only are the monk’s sandals much shorter ([b]barely going above the ankle[/b]), than the barbarian’s boots (almost[b] reaching up to the knee[/b]), but the barbarian’s boots are also much thicker than the monk’s sandals! Now, what would happen if we simply swapped out the barbarian’s boots with the monk’s sandals? 

By default, if we would swap out the boots with the sandals, there would be [b]missing information[/b] for the shin region, leading to a rather disturbing result: 

[img]https://www.txkgaming.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/image-5-1024x749.png[/img][i]The barbarian is wearing the monk's sandals... but wait: the barbarian's pants aren't made for this![/i]

 Of course, the [b]easiest solution[/b] here would be to simply[b] disallow shoes to come in different sizes[/b]! That would mean [b]creating a system where all clothing pieces are of the same size[/b].

While a system like this would fix the problem and is also [b]commonly used in other games,[/b] we wanted to push the amount of flexibility not only for our artists but also for the players, when designing their characters. So that [b]we can allow a wider variety of character designs[/b]: 

[img]https://txkgaming.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/MonkZonesComparedwBoxes-1024x655.png[/img][i]Different Concepts > Different Zones[/i]

So, after investing some time into R&D we came up with a much more [b]flexible solution:[/b]

[b]Layered Clothing[/b] 

By creating a layered clothing system, we allowed our clothing assets to be created [b]independently[/b] of the region's sizes.

That means that our[b] artists can create overlapping clothing pieces[/b] (e.g., very high boots, very long pants) and [b]dynamically cut away the unwanted areas of each clothing piece depending on the other equipped clothes.[/b] 

Normally overlapping clothes create frequent clipping (see image below), but by tagging each component with identifiers as well as a thickness level, we can compare these thickness levels and [b]cut away the thinner component.[/b]

In the following example, the boots are thicker than the pants, so the pants should be tucked into the boots. Without a layered clothing system, the pants and boots would look like this: 

[img]https://txkgaming.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/image.png[/img]
[i]The pants and boots are “clipping” into each other[/i]

In our case, the layered clothing system that we have created [b]automatically hides[/b] the pants at the region, where they would intersect!

[img]https://www.txkgaming.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/image-3-1024x831.png[/img][i]The pants are tucked inside the boots[/i]

While this looks quite simple, the system actually needs to do quite A LOT of [b]technical-art-magic<sup>tm</sup>[/b] to handle all the edge cases that come along with the layered clothing (What happens if you have skin showing through a clothing piece? What happens to assets that vary in thickness [b]within[/b] their own region: e.g., a knight’s gauntlet that has very thick hand elements but only thin cloth elements above the wrist?)

Nevertheless, our team was able to overcome all of those challenges and we are very happy with the current pipeline and its flexibility regarding layered clothing. [b]Awesome job everyone! [/b]

However, with this issue solved, there was yet another main problem to be tackled: 
[h2][b]Performance[/b][/h2]
“This all sounds very cool and customizable but will it run without burning through my graphics card?” you may ask. 

It is very true that [b]performance is critical[/b], especially for VR games. Thus, a lot of thought went into the process of optimizing our characters and their clothing. Given that optimization is a [b]completely[/b] different topic in itself, we want to focus on the main bottleneck with this system: [b]Draw calls.[/b] 

[b][u]“What are draw calls?” [/u]I hear you asking.[/b] 

A great indicator of the performance cost is how often the [b]CPU [/b](Processor) [b]has to tell the GPU [/b](Graphics Card) how and where to draw meshes on the screen, usually referred to as “draw calls”. Since those commands to the GPU are quite expensive, when it comes to performance, you try to [b]reduce[/b] them as much as possible. 

Now, that our characters are made up of almost dozens of individual meshes, stitched together, you can already see where the problem is: Our character who [b]was just 1 draw call [/b]before now needs over 10 draw calls for each of their regions! Additionally, each “material” (the textures that give colors and patterns to our character) requires 1 additional draw call, leading to [b]a sum of around 20 draw calls! [/b] 

This means with [b]10 characters[/b] on screen we would have [b]almost 200 draw calls instead of 20[/b] (including draw calls for the materials)! 

While the example above is quite simplified the main issue is clear: [b]we need to reduce the draw calls! [/b] 

[b]So, what did we do? [/b] 

We were able to lower the number of draw calls to a minimum by [b]combining the textures and meshes[/b] of our character. This means that instead of one or more draw calls for every region (which would be the case if every region had its very own texture or mesh), the CPU issues [b]just two draw call[/b] for the whole character!

This combining does come at a cost though! While the [b]runtime performance[/b] (when actively playing) [b]is much better now[/b], the actual combining and merging of the character are fairly resource intense, which means additional loading times. However, the process of combining meshes and textures happens within the CPU itself. We can actively optimize it and run those calculations in parallel for a [b]significantly better performance! [/b] 

The result is a much more efficient character editor that can craft performant characters with [b]little to no loading times. [/b]

We could continue for hours about various technical details and optimizations that we deployed (like our solution for optimizing textures), however, given the length of this post already (comment [u]“Rolling constitution saving throw!” [/u]if you are still reading!) we will end this community update on this note. 

Nevertheless, we hope that this insight wasn’t too technical for you and that you enjoyed reading about our character editor! Of course, [b]we will be[/b] [b]active on Discord for feedback, questions, and just, in general, hanging out with you guys! [/b]

And if you haven't already: Don't forget to [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1710740/Dungeon_Full_Dive/]wishlist DfD on Steam[/url] to support the development team! 

Thank you very much for reading this community update, and as always:

We are truly looking forward to seeing you inside DFD!

[b]- Your TxK Gaming Team [/b]

notes.title: Our Character Editor! #1 - Developer Update
notes.content:
Greetings Travelers!

Welcome back to our latest developer update, where we give you a peek behind the curtains of development! In the last months, we have been heavily focusing on the	[b]		 map builder	[/b]	 as well as the	[b]		 character editor[/b]. Both of these topics are incredibly exciting for us to work on, and they both deserve a spot on their own in our developer updates.

	For this update, however, we want to take a [b]deeper look at our character editor[/b]. The reason for this is, that the work on the map builder has been strongly centered around optimization and improving our existing map asset pipeline: Technical essentials — that will enable us to make the most out of the players' hardware — which are, however, too technical for the moment (we will go into detail there, once the user-facing features are ready to be shown off as well!).

	So, without further ado, thank you for your patience, and let's start with this developer update!


[h1]	[b]		 Whether it's crawling through a dungeon or dancing at the queen's ball...	[/b][/h1]
	[b]		 ...our adventurers want to be dressed for the occasion!	[/b]

	This was our highest priority when we set up our character art pipeline. We want to allow players to not only equip different prebuilt outfits but to actually	[b]		 mix and match different, individual clothing pieces[/b] !

	Having this goal in mind we had to solve quite a lot of challenges. One of the biggest was defining a	[b]		 gorgeous-looking, visual artstyle	[/b]	 for our characters, while at the same time meeting the	[b]		 strict performance goals	[/b]	 that we have set up, to ensure a good performance for all our players.

	So how did we do it? For the sake of readability, we broke down the results of our work into two main parts for you:

	·	[b]		 #1 The visual art challenge:	[/b]	 Bringing your heroes to life

	And

	·	[b]		 #2 The development & technical art challenge:	[/b]	 Our clothing system


[h1]	#1 Bringing your heroes to life	[b]		 - An insight into the artstyle of our characters	[/b][/h1]
	Initially, when we started on the concepts for our characters and their outfits, we spent a lot of time finding the right level of	[b]		 stylization	[/b]	 and	[b]		 detail[/b]. We wanted our heroes to be the	[b]		 highlights of our fantasy worlds	[/b]	 and yet perfectly fit into the style of the environments.

	During the course of our conception phase, a	[b]		 wide variety of explorations and concepts[/b]	 had to be created, in order to get many different variations for our internal testing. Through this testing, we succeeded in achieving a fantastic final art style that we are proud to show off to you.

	So, let's accompany	[b]		 Dungeon Full Dive's barbarian outfit	[/b]	 on its journey through our character pipeline	[b]		 from concept art to 3D[/b]!

[h1]	2D - Exploration & Concept[/h1]
	The exploration phase is the first stage of conception, in which we	[b]		 wildly explore what is possible	[/b]	 for the outfit. This is done before we actually decide on a certain design that we want to implement. The results here are far from the final detailed design, and more focused on the	[b]		 general elements	[/b]	 that we want to have as well as the	[b]		 overall design[/b]. Things like the	[b]		 characters' silhouettes	[/b]	 are also very important during this stage!

	[b]		 Exploration	[/b]

	[img]https://ksr-ugc.imgix.net/assets/038/271/087/c47109f19a39b7ee6d525a56877a52a7_original.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.0.2&w=700&fit=max&v=1660473092&gif-q=50&q=92&s=62302b165ef6e1e6383c84b967c31b07[/img]	[u]		 
The first explorations are focused on finding the right clothing pieces and the overall design that we want to have.	[/u]

	[b]		 Concept	[/b]

	After we decide on the final elements for the outfit, our concept artists proceed with creating a first rendered concept art:

	[img]https://ksr-ugc.imgix.net/assets/038/271/027/6a308ef8994a22556bb1a32bdc939c4e_original.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.0.2&w=700&fit=max&v=1660471887&gif-q=50&q=92&s=cf2acda17c4de7e8e9937bed6cfb0b80[/img]	[u]		 
A more youthful look and pants! You can also see some explorations and thoughts on clothes, materials, and different armor pieces.	[/u]

	The further we proceed with the pipeline and the more we transition from 2D concept art towards the 3D plane, the more we have to consider the details of the design. When making a 3D character something very crucial comes into play:	[b]		 technical limitations	[/b]	 as well as the	[b]		 readability of the design[/b].

	That is why we must have an eye on things like the level of detail:

	[img]https://ksr-ugc.imgix.net/assets/038/271/109/75b26c5fefa0d9d3f72db15feeeae526_original.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.0.2&w=700&fit=max&v=1660473500&gif-q=50&q=92&s=7b08c0f9b13eb7602369a9432d33f5a4[/img]	[u]		
 More is not always better!	[/u]
[h1]	[b]		 3D	[/b]	 - Sculpting, Modeling & Texturing[/h1]
	[b]		 Sculpting	[/b]

	Next, based on the 2D concept, our 3D artists are able to sculpt a first model:

	[img]https://ksr-ugc.imgix.net/assets/038/271/137/e386cccd4cf010cafe65b85a7b7c0659_original.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.0.2&w=700&fit=max&v=1660474212&gif-q=50&q=92&s=fdf80e89d6c80850354617b5b3bbd0e6[/img]	[u]		 
The first translation in 3D with simple colors, to help with the visualization.	[/u]

	[b]		 Texturing	[/b]

	With a 3D model in place, we are able to texture the character. That means giving him color and bringing the materials to life!

	[img]https://ksr-ugc.imgix.net/assets/038/271/148/68b03f01a667bfacf995d996f95928e6_original.png?ixlib=rb-4.0.2&w=700&fit=max&v=1660474393&gif-q=50&lossless=true&s=774dc50c5be68385084aa2923db4ef27[/img]	[u]		 
We finally got a model we like! Nice! Unfortunately, we are not done yet. Now that we have the first version, we start on the details with lots of feedback from the other artists and developers.	[/u]

	Of course, during all of these steps, we also go through a feedback & polishing loop. The feedback & polishing is crucial for our artists, to	[b]		 reach our targeted visual goals[/b]! This is one example of such a feedback loop for the barbarian outfit:

	[img]https://ksr-ugc.imgix.net/assets/038/268/325/402840cef146706ac0b9bface6aaab6b_original.png?ixlib=rb-4.0.2&w=700&fit=max&v=1660429416&gif-q=50&lossless=true&s=8e67c9a87b4cb1679925cee11878dde8[/img]	[u]		 
There is a lot of thought and work that has to go into the creation of our characters!	[/u]

	After we review and discuss the changes, we can work them in, and our barbarian looks like this:

	[img]https://ksr-ugc.imgix.net/assets/038/268/328/4078f3faa697d7f6ff54c87ccc287761_original.png?ixlib=rb-4.0.2&w=700&fit=max&v=1660429453&gif-q=50&lossless=true&s=d9bd21835562eb19cd7168e8c8fbcd4c[/img]	[u]		
 Even more handsome, don't you think?	[/u]

	Now we can finalize the textures ...and add the final details!

	[img]https://ksr-ugc.imgix.net/assets/038/271/477/097d793b0e7c1f3bf84eee0618653014_original.jpg?ixlib=rb-4.0.2&w=700&fit=max&v=1660479062&gif-q=50&q=92&s=489d77da0177fc1ed1cfc2c0f52eb6c9[/img]	[u]		 
And there you go: Our barbarian is ready for the character editor, awesome! ... But what happened to the boots? This is explained in our technical-art-insight-post regarding the clothing system!	[/u]

	In summary, our outfits have to go through	[b]		 a lot of different stages	[/b]	 before being ready for the game: from exploration to the	[b]		 concept[/b], to	[b]		 sculpting[/b],	[b]		 texturing[/b], the	[b]		 feedback loop[/b], and final	[b]		 polishing!	[/b]

	[img]https://www.txkgaming.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/FinalResult-1024x325.jpg[/img]	[u]		[u]			 As you can see, the design of the barbarian can drastically improve from one step to the next! And there are even more steps that we have not shown here for the sake of simplicity (like retopologizing, UV-layout, etc.). Making video games can be a tough job!		[/u]	[/u]

	I hope we were able to give you an	[b]		 insight	[/b]	 and understanding	[b]		 into our work[/b]! Keeping the length of this post and your reading pleasure in mind, we will have to continue the second part of this post in a separate community update. But worry not! It's already prepared and will be posted	[b]		 in the next weeks	[/b]	 ;)

	So, stay tuned for	[b]		 part 2[/b]: "The development & tech-art challenge: Our clothing system"

	In the meantime, feel free to let us know in the comments:	[b]		 What do you think of the design? What is the next class that you want to see?	[/b]

	And as always: We are truly looking forward to seeing you inside DFD!

	- Your TxK Gaming Team
